o1.biggest_strength: Tight, on-brand emails built on the right segment, the pricing trigger and the rev rec rebuild pain, with no links. It adds practical extras: reply handling, an opt-out footer and an A/B test.
o1.biggest_mistake: The 12th-to-15th start window can hold a fresh pricing flag for up to a month, which works against the weekly trigger. It also says 'leave out about 4,100' while only loading flagged contacts, so the real load size is never stated.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Send within days of each weekly flag instead of on a fixed monthly window. State how many flagged Controllers we can realistically expect per week, and turn that into a meetings number.

o2.biggest_strength: The expectations section is honest and fully worked out: it plans on 6.8%, deliberately does not multiply the two gains, and its 1,900-contact math checks out (about 130 replies, 65 positive, 55 meetings). It also gives a clear weekly load-on-flag rule.
o2.biggest_mistake: Step 2 slips into a product pitch ('Chargebee is built so...'). It also leaves out pilot Controllers, who are not on the new list, and the full-1,900 projection quietly assumes every one of them gets a pricing flag.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Cut the product line in step 2. Size the weekly flagged volume realistically rather than assuming all 1,900 fire. Add an opt-out footer and a plan for handling replies.

reason: Both nailed the segment, the trigger and the no-link rule. I'd take 2 because it times sends to the weekly flag and gives me reply math I can actually defend, though 1's emails are slightly cleaner.
